selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What happens in the sky at the time of 'Isha in this passage?
questions.answer: The last light of day disappears, and night covers the world.

questions.question: What does the passing of time do to the works left behind by those who are gone?
questions.answer: It removes their traces from this world.

questions.question: What bigger truth does that fading away remind people of?
questions.answer: It reminds them that living things pass from this world into another world.

questions.question: How is this world described when it is compared with the hereafter?
questions.answer: This world is shown as small, temporary, and low, while the hereafter is wide, lasting, and majestic.

questions.question: Who alone deserves to own, manage, love, and be worshipped in the universe?
questions.answer: Allah alone deserves that.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only Allah can be the true object of worship?
questions.answer: Because He easily changes huge things, like night and day, winter and spring, and this world and the next.

questions.question: What picture is used to show how easily Allah changes things?
questions.answer: The passage says it is like turning the pages of a book.

questions.question: What two actions with the pages of a book are compared to Allah’s power over creation?
questions.answer: Writing and erasing.

questions.question: What main lesson about 'Isha does this part teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that 'Isha is a time to remember Allah’s power, the passing of this world, and the reality of the hereafter.

questions.question: If Allah can make all these changes, what should a believer understand about Him?
questions.answer: A believer should understand that Allah has complete power and alone deserves worship.

questions.question: At nightfall, what disappears from the horizon?
questions.answer: The last signs of daytime disappear.

questions.question: After the day ends, what fills the universe?
questions.answer: The world of night spreads over it.

questions.question: Which seasonal change is mentioned along with the change from day to night?
questions.answer: The change from summer to winter.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention old traces being wiped away over time?
questions.answer: To show that things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: What does this teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that this life is temporary and leads to another life.

questions.question: What event connected to this world is described in a very serious and frightening way?
questions.answer: The end of this world is described as a terrible dying.

questions.question: What appears after the destruction of this passing world?
questions.answer: The great and everlasting world of the hereafter appears.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability to make changes?
questions.answer: It says He makes great changes with ease.

questions.question: Name one pair of opposites in the passage that Allah changes into each other.
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: How should this passage shape a Muslim student’s understanding of worship?
questions.answer: It should help the student see that worship belongs only to Allah, who has power over everything and whose hereafter is everlasting.

questions.question: What time of day is the target passage about?
questions.answer: It is about the time of 'Isha, at nightfall.

questions.question: What natural change begins this passage?
questions.answer: Daylight fades away and night takes over.

questions.question: How does the passage help us think about Allah’s control of the world?
questions.answer: It points to the changes Allah brings in time, seasons, life, and worlds.

questions.question: What season is described as green and decorated?
questions.answer: Summer.
